ns2:course.label: Hispanics in the U.S.
ns2:course.description: Hispanics constitute a growing population in the United States. The size and heterogeneity of Hispanics raises complex issues in crafting public policy and in designing and delivering social services. This course offers an extensive portrait of Hispanics in the United States. Students will explore questions and demographic characteristics, language and religious practices, education, criminal justice, neighborhood and economic restructuring, immigration, social service systems, and community action in the context of creating an effective public policy agenda. Same as LLS 412.
ns2:course.sectionRegistrationNotes: Not intended for students with Freshman or Sophomore class standing. Restricted to BSW: Social Work - UIUC.
